newsitem.title: VATICAN: Historian of Vatican policy towards Nazis dies.
newsitem.headline: Historian of Vatican policy towards Nazis dies.

text.p: Father Robert Graham, one of the Roman Catholic Church's foremost experts on the Vatican's policy towards Nazi Germany, has died at 85, Vatican Radio reported on Friday.
The Jesuit died on Monday in Los Gatos, California near his native San Francisco, the radio said, giving no cause of death.
Graham had returned home last year after working for three decades in Rome as an historian of Church and Vatican activity during World War Two.

A strong defender of wartime Pope Pius XII, who has been criticised for not doing enough to help Jews during the Nazi era, Graham published numerous books as well as articles in the Jesuit review Civita Cattolica (Catholic Civilisation).
"Father Graham became famous not only for his competence, acquired in years of work in archives all over the world, but also for his sincerity of intent," Vatican Radio said.
"Anyone who met him...knew he was solely seeking the historical truth."

Graham long argued that Pius XII had worked quietly behind the scenes to save Jews and did not speak out more forcefully for fear of merely worsening the situation for Catholics as well as Jews in Germany and German-occupied countries.
He told Reuters in an interview last year that 2,000 priests had been detained in Dachau and Pius XII made no appeal for them or for detained Jews for fear of reprisals.
"He (Pope Pius) did not give speeches. For the Pope to make speeches would not have helped. It would have compromised the position of Jews and Catholics," Graham said.
